note:
2026-09-29 remeasurement against the pinned v1.1.23+5adf783 compiler and current authenticated-field implementation. The two highest-cardinality Q16/Q17 rows no longer measure direct whole-field walks, because both routes are now bounded: step-06 caps its direct walk at 64 script witnesses (3e3090aa1; wider fields take the staged step-07/step-08 scan) and step-04 scans 32 address witnesses per step with a checkpoint (c2237b30). The rows were re-pointed at those bounded steps, both fit the unchanged execution basis, and their judgements therefore move to `fits`. Their retired infeasibility text described single-step direct walks at 224 and 318 witnesses (35,584,117 and 40,237,813 mem, ~2.7x and ~3.0x the memory basis). Those figures remain the measured reason for docs/spec/midgard-tx.md §8.3 erratum E2 constraint 1, that a direct whole-field walk at the admissible maximum does not fit, which is why both routes are bounded. These are paired harness execution readings, not complete signed-transaction or carriage-fit claims. The historical notes below describe their original source/compiler state, not current costs.

The Q1x lane's rolling re-measurement, attached as a lane exit criterion per #565's measurement-slotting rule. Regenerate with `MIDGARD_AIKEN_BIN=<fork> node scripts/verify-q1x-exec-ledger-v1.mjs --update`, and move any reported number in the same commit. Provisional: formal closure of #551 is Phase 7's, against the Phase-6 blueprint. `--update` rewrites raw rows, derived figures and the Q1X-F6 growth readings; it does NOT rewrite `basisFit`, `infeasibility`, `errata` or the Q1X-F6 bands, because those are judgements and a re-take must not be able to launder one. `--update` is also not a bypass: structural failures (a selector that did not run, a missing block, a judgement the fresh measurement contradicts, a Q1X-F6 band the fresh reading falls outside) fail in update mode too and the ledger is not rewritten.

**#584 re-take.** Every measured row here rose by a fixed **per-opening** amount when #584 gave `field_opening_v1` a multi-field opening: the single-field `opened_field_view`/`opened_field_walk` are now `anchored_native_tx` followed by `anchored_field_view`/`anchored_field_walk`, so a one-field step pays one extra opaque-record construction, the field reads that go with it, plus the two separate `expect`s `field_pairs_with` now spends so that a refusal names which guard fired rather than only that the field did not pair. The amount is not one number but two, because the two §2.5 halves construct different handles: **+7,117 mem / +2,529,845 cpu** on the Q10/Q11 body-field rows (field 0, opened as a `BodyTxOpening`, whose handle carries this module's unread placeholder witness set) and **+7,580 mem / +2,673,308 cpu** on the Q16/Q17 witness-field rows (fields 6 and 7, opened as a `WitnessTxOpening`, which additionally carries the transaction's real `NativeTxWitnessSetCompact` and pays the anchored `witness_set_hash` equality). Each amount reappears unchanged in the derived subtraction under it, and the four control rows — which never reach the door — did not move at all. What carries the per-opening conclusion is that within each half the shift is identical on the low- and high-cardinality rows: it is per-opening, not per-item. It therefore moves no growth figure (`memoryGrowth`/`cpuGrowth` are unchanged; only the headroom readings shift) and no `basisFit`, and the larger of the two is under 0.06% of the §3.3 memory basis and under 0.04% of the cpu basis. The alternative was a second spelling of `carriage_reaches_the_anchor` and the §2.5 body/witness pairing for the single-field path, which the AGENTS.md tradeoff order (correctness, safety, liveness, performance) does not buy at that price.

**#586 re-take.** The four door rows — Q11 step-02 and Q10 step-04, each at 1 and at 296 spend inputs — rose by **+1,312 mem / +358,482 cpu** apiece, and nothing else in the ledger moved: the four control rows did not, and neither did the Q16/Q17 witness-field rows. The cause is #586's §5.3 ledger-key width guard: `decode_midgard_tx_input_cbor` in `lib/midgard/fraud-proofs/native-tx/components.ak` now asserts an input item is **exactly** 38 bytes (`midgard_tx_input_item_bytes`) before reading anything, so the non-minimal 39-byte spelling `82 ‖ 59 0020 ‖ tx_id(32) ‖ 19 index_be16` — which `decode_definite_bytes_at` on its own accepts as the same `(tx_id, output_index)` — is refused, and one out-ref has one trie key. The cost is that one length equality, so it is **per execution that decodes an out-ref, not per item**: the shift is identical on the low- and high-cardinality rows, and the Q16/Q17 rows walk fields 6 and 7 and decode no input item. Being the same on both rows of a subtraction pair, it cancels out of the growth figures — `memoryGrowth`/`cpuGrowth` are unchanged at -112,081 and -4,947,358 — and it reappears unchanged in each derived row; only the headroom readings move (12,827,679 → 12,826,367 mem, 7,851,416,297 → 7,851,057,815 cpu, both still above 97% of the §3.3 basis). It moves no `basisFit`, no `infeasibility` figure and no Q1X-F6 band, and +1,312 is under 0.01% of the §3.3 memory basis.

**#592 round-4 re-take, §8.3 erratum E1's repair of `K` (15,900 → 15,148).** `chunk_bytes_k` is compiled into `native_tx_field_access_v1`, which every step here reaches through the §8.8 door, so every row that opens a field rose by one fixed **per-door-opening** amount — and, as in the #584 and #586 re-takes above, the amount is not one number but two, split the same way the two §2.5 halves are: **+2,224 mem / +682,801 cpu** on the Q10/Q11 body-field rows (field 0, opened as a `BodyTxOpening`) and **+2,124 mem / +666,801 cpu** on the Q16/Q17 witness-field rows (fields 6 and 7, opened as a `WitnessTxOpening`). Within each half the shift is identical at one item and at the admissible maximum, which is what makes it per-opening rather than per-item, and none of the control rows — which never reach the door — moved at all. The derived rows below are not readings of a second opening: each is the control-subtraction of one single-opening row, so with the controls unmoved each derived figure shifts by exactly its own row's amount (+2,224 / +682,801 under the Q10/Q11 rows, +2,124 / +666,801 under the Q16/Q17 rows). Nothing about these steps changed — the movement is the door's own `expected_chunk_count` / chunk-offset arithmetic running against the repaired divisor. No `basisFit`, no `infeasibility` string and no Q1X-F6 band moved, and the fresh readings all fall inside their recorded bands, which is what `--update` refuses to launder.

**#606 re-take, 2026-08-16 — the E2 certificate repair, and a normative correction the numbers did not cause.** Bisected against pristine `git archive` builds of the intervening commits rather than assumed: the pexcludes rider `139a8ca3` leaves every row below identical to the batch base `854fea09` to the unit, so the whole of the movement is the E2 repair commit `d528e00b` — constant certificate asset name, mint-welded `field_hash`, the door's new equality of that `field_hash` against the commitment derived from the anchored structures, and the deletion of `carriage_reaches_the_anchor`.

The cost half is small and structured. **All eight measured rows moved; all eight control rows did not move by a unit.** The shift is one amount per step and it is *identical at both cardinalities of that step*, which is what makes it per-execution rather than per-item: Q11 step-02 **−2,567 mem / −770,914 cpu** at 1 and at 296 spend inputs alike, Q10 step-04 **−2,067 / −690,914**, Q16 step-04 **−2,367 / −738,914** at 1 and at 318 address witnesses, and Q17 step-06 **+2,633 / +61,086** at 1 and at 224 script witnesses. The signs differ across steps and no per-opening rate is claimed from them: `d528e00b` deleted one per-field guard and added one door equality, and these four readings do not separate the two.

Because each subtraction pair moved by the same amount on both of its rows, **every figure this ledger derives from a pair is unchanged to the unit**: `memoryGrowth`/`cpuGrowth` at −112,081 and −4,947,358, and both infeasibility marginals — ~156,800 mem and ~52,400,000 cpu per script witness, ~125,100 mem and ~39,900,000 cpu per address witness — and therefore the ~81-witness and ~101-witness execution limits derived from them. Only the headroom readings move, to 12,826,210 mem and 7,851,065,928 cpu, both still above 97% of the §3.3 basis. No `basisFit`, no `errata` and no Q1X-F6 band moved, and the fresh readings fall inside their recorded bands — which is the check `--update` refuses to launder.

**The correction that is not about cost.** Three `infeasibility` narratives in this ledger asserted that tier-3 carriage is refused outright for the witness-set fields under §8.3 erratum E2 limit 3, and that resolution of that refusal was owed by #579. **#606 RESOLVED limit 3** (owner ruling 2026-08-16): the §8.6 certificate datum carries a mint-welded `field_hash`, the door requires it to equal the commitment derived from the anchored structures, `carriage_reaches_the_anchor` was deleted, and tier 3 is admissible at every field including 6–8. Left as they stood, this ledger and §8.3 of the spec it cross-references would contradict each other on this batch's central normative claim. The three narratives are re-stated in place, each keeping the sentence it replaced verbatim so the change is legible rather than silent. **No measured figure moves with the correction**, and neither does either limit: E2 limits 1 and 2 stand, these rows are limit 1, and limit 1 was never a carriage limit — what the correction removes is a *second* reason that was being given for a conclusion execution already carries on its own.

q1xF6.defect: #551 — Q10/Q11 exceeded the ledger memory cap at the admissible spend-input cardinality because the step reproduced the whole authenticated collection to re-hash it. Measured then: Q10 step-04 fit the 20% reserve only to 39 inputs, Q11 step-02 to 40, and at 296 neither proof could be evaluated.
q1xF6.claim: Under the §8.8 door the step's cost does not scale with the disputed transaction's spend-input count: the preimage is hashed once (§7.1) and item n is located by §5.3 arithmetic (§10.5).
q1xF6.lowCardinalityClaim: Q10 double-spend step-04 at 1 spend input
q1xF6.highCardinalityClaim: Q10 double-spend step-04 at 296 spend inputs
q1xF6.toleranceRationale: The door pays one blake2b_256 over a preimage that does grow with cardinality - 43 bytes at one input, 11,843 at 296 - so the honest growth is the hash of ~11.8 KB more and nothing else, measured at ~4,600 mem. The band has to hold that plus the control-subtraction artifact described in `deltaAttribution` (|171,081| mem, |14,387,358| cpu), and has to sit far below any per-item regression. Both were measured rather than assumed: a step regressed to walk the whole 296-item collection costs +25,127,050 mem / +8,363,297,421 cpu against the same control, and one regressed to walk only half of it +12,129,016 mem / +4,062,287,469 cpu. The bands below are therefore ~1.5x (mem) and ~7x (cpu) the observed artifact, which now uses about 68% of the memory band, and ~48x (mem) and ~40x (cpu) below the cheapest regression measured, so neither a half-collection walk nor anything dearer can hide inside them. cpu is carried as its own two-sided band because it is the axis a walk regression moves proportionally hardest against its own tolerance.
q1xF6.deltaAttribution: The measured growth is negative on both axes (-171,081 mem, -14,387,358 cpu). That is not the step getting cheaper with cardinality - execution units are deterministic integers and a step whose only cardinality-dependent work is one hash over a larger preimage cannot cost less at 296 inputs than at 1. The cause is the subtraction, not the step. A control row and a measured row are two separately compiled UPLC programs that happen to share source for the fixture; Aiken inlines and prunes each against its own uses, so the shared prefix is not compiled identically in the two, and the difference between them is the validator's cost PLUS a compilation difference over a fixture whose own cost is cardinality-dependent. That residue is what the negative sign is. It was localised rather than asserted: an isolated pair of probes around `verify_native_tx_compact_cbor_v1` alone - a function whose entire input is the 2.5 compact structure, which is nine field commitments plus fixed scalars and therefore the SAME LENGTH at both cardinalities (pinned by the neutralisation selector `q1x_f6_compact_structure_length_is_cardinality_independent`) - measured 195,736 mem at 1 input and 77,736 at 296 by exactly this style of subtraction. A function that cannot vary with cardinality 'varied' by -118,000 mem and -18,880,000 cpu, which is the whole of the anomaly and then some. What the rows do establish, and establish decisively, is the bound: the step costs 492,127 mem at one input and 321,046 at 296, both under 3.8% of the 13,200,000 basis, where the retired idiom could not be evaluated at 296 at all. The exact-equality pins make any future movement visible; the two-sided bands make a movement that matters fail.
